findings.title: Schema initialization does not migrate existing admin-permissions clients to the new Clients type/scopes
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. This PR adds the Clients resource type and new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite), but realms that already initialized the admin permissions client with the previous Users-only schema will never get the new scopes or the 'Clients' all-resource. Subsequent client-permission creation or evaluation can fail with validation errors such as missing scopes, or with null type-resource lookups. An idempotent schema sync/migration is needed when the schema changes.

findings.title: Removed-client cleanup is not handled for V2 and may throw when V1 and V2 are both enabled
findings.body: registerListener is now gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1), but AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If only V2 is enabled, ClientRemovedEvent is ignored and authorization resources/permissions created for the removed client are left orphaned. If V1 and V2 are both enabled, the listener calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing client-removal event processing to fail. V2 needs its own cleanup path or the listener must explicitly avoid unsupported V2 calls.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type-resource name instead of client IDs
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission iterates all resources of type 'Clients', which includes the schema's all-resource named 'Clients'. When a type-wide permission grants the requested scope, hasGrantedPermission returns true for that all-resource and the method adds the literal string "Clients" to the returned set. The method contract is to return client identifiers; it neither expands a type-wide grant to actual client IDs nor filters out the type resource. Callers using this set to filter or query clients may miss all clients covered by a type-wide permission or include an invalid identifier.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve display names for Clients resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName was not updated for the newly added Clients resource type. It only special-cases Users; for Clients it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources created by getOrCreateResource are named by the client's database ID and do not have a display name set, so policy/evaluation representations will expose null or a non-human-readable name for client resources.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new map-roles-client-scope permission
findings.body: The PR adds the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles, but the added tests only exercise MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. There is no integration test verifying that a MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission allows mapping client roles to client scopes, so this new authorization path is untested.
